questions.questionTextEn: The octahedral complex $[\text{Rh}(\text{py})_3\text{Cl}_3]$ ($\text{py} =$ pyridine) exists as two geometrical isomers, *fac* and *mer*. Their point groups are, respectively,
questions.explanationEn: Ignoring internal rotation of the pyridine rings (treating each ligand as a point donor), *fac*-[$\text{M}\text{A}_3\text{B}_3$] places three identical ligands on one triangular face of the octahedron, giving a $C_3$ axis and three vertical mirror planes ($C_{3v}$). In *mer*-[$\text{M}\text{A}_3\text{B}_3$], the three identical ligands lie in a meridional plane, giving a $C_2$ axis and two vertical mirror planes ($C_{2v}$).

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Coordination Chemistry & f-Block Elements (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: In an octahedral transition metal complex $\text{ML}_6$, $\pi$-donor ligands such as $\text{Br}^-$ decrease the magnitude of $\Delta_o$ primarily by
optionsEn: raising the energy of the ligand $a_{1g}$ orbitals
raising the energy of the metal $t_{2g}$ orbitals through $\pi$-antibonding interaction
lowering the energy of the metal $e_g^*$ orbitals
lowering the energy of the metal $t_{2g}$ orbitals through $\pi$-bonding interaction
questions.explanationEn: Filled ligand $\pi$-donor orbitals of $t_{2g}$ symmetry lie lower in energy than the metal $t_{2g}$ $d$-orbitals. Their interaction produces a lower-energy ligand-centered bonding $t_{2g}$ set and a higher-energy metal-centered antibonding $t_{2g}^*$ set. Pushing the metal $t_{2g}^*$ orbitals upward narrows the gap to $e_g^*$, thereby decreasing $\Delta_o$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Coordination Chemistry & f-Block Elements (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: For which of the following high-spin octahedral complexes is the experimental room-temperature magnetic moment ($\mu_{\text{eff}}$) expected to be SIGNIFICANTLY HIGHER than the spin-only value ($\mu_{\text{so}}$) due to first-order orbital angular momentum contribution?
questions.explanationEn: First-order orbital contribution occurs in octahedral complexes with an orbitally triply degenerate $T$ ground state (asymmetrically occupied $t_{2g}$ orbitals). High-spin $[\text{Co}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{2+}$ ($t_{2g}^5 e_g^2$, $^4T_{1g}$) retains substantial orbital angular momentum, raising $\mu_{\text{eff}}$ to $4.7\text{--}5.2\text{ BM}$ versus $\mu_{\text{so}} = 3.87\text{ BM}$. The other three have $A$-type ground states ($^4A_{2g}$, $^6A_{1g}$, $^3A_{2g}$) with quenched first-order orbital momentum.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Coordination Chemistry & f-Block Elements (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Starting from $[\text{PtCl}_4]^{2-}$, the sequential addition of $2\text{ equiv.}$ of $\text{NH}_3$ followed by $2\text{ equiv.}$ of $\text{PPh}_3$ (or treating $[\text{Pt}(\text{NH}_3)_4]^{2+}$ with $2\text{ equiv.}$ of $\text{Cl}^-$) gives distinct isomers. Specifically, reacting $[\text{Pt}(\text{NH}_3)_4]^{2+}$ with $2\text{ equiv.}$ of $\text{Cl}^-$ yields
questions.explanationEn: The first $\text{Cl}^-$ replaces any $\text{NH}_3$ to give $[\text{Pt}(\text{NH}_3)_3\text{Cl}]^+$. Because $\text{Cl}^-$ has a stronger trans effect than $\text{NH}_3$ ($\text{Cl}^- > \text{NH}_3$), the $\text{NH}_3$ ligand *trans* to $\text{Cl}^-$ is labilized and selectively replaced by the second $\text{Cl}^-$, yielding $\text{trans}-[\text{Pt}(\text{NH}_3)_2\text{Cl}_2]$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Coordination Chemistry & f-Block Elements (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: In the linear uranyl ion, $[\text{UO}_2]^{2+}$, the formal oxidation state of uranium and the number of $5f$ electrons on uranium are, respectively,
questions.explanationEn: Each oxo ligand ($\text{O}^{2-}$) carries a $-2$ charge, so for $[\text{UO}_2]^{2+}$ the oxidation state of uranium is $x + 2(-2) = +2 \implies x = +6$. Since neutral uranium ($Z = 92$) has the configuration $[\text{Rn}]5f^3 6d^1 7s^2$, removing $6$ electrons gives $\text{U}^{6+}$ with a closed-shell $[\text{Rn}]5f^0$ configuration ($0$ $5f$ electrons).

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Coordination Chemistry & f-Block Elements (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Identify the correct statement(s) regarding $\sigma$- and $\pi$-bonding in octahedral transition metal complexes:
optionsEn: $\pi$-Acceptor ligands such as $\text{CO}$ and $\text{CN}^-$ stabilize the metal $t_{2g}$ orbitals and increase $\Delta_o$
$\pi$-Donor ligands such as $\text{Cl}^-$ and $\text{I}^-$ destabilize the metal $t_{2g}$ orbitals and decrease $\Delta_o$
The metal $e_g$ orbitals ($d_{z^2}, d_{x^2-y^2}$) participate in both $\sigma$- and $\pi$-bonding with monodentate ligands in $O_h$ symmetry
Increasing the metal oxidation state from $+2$ to $+3$ for the same metal and ligands generally increases $\Delta_o$
questions.explanationEn: (A) True: empty ligand $\pi^*$ orbitals of $t_{2g}$ symmetry lower the metal $t_{2g}$ level, increasing $\Delta_o$. (B) True: filled ligand $\pi$ orbitals raise metal $t_{2g}^*$, decreasing $\Delta_o$. (C) False: in $O_h$ symmetry, ligand $\pi$-SALCs transform as $T_{1g} + T_{2g} + T_{1u} + T_{2u}$, which does NOT include $E_g$, so metal $e_g$ orbitals engage only in $\sigma$-bonding. (D) True: higher positive charge pulls ligands closer, increasing $\Delta_o$ by roughly $40\text{--}80\%$. Hence (A), (B), and (D) are correct.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Coordination Chemistry & f-Block Elements (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statements about trivalent lanthanide ions ($\text{Ln}^{3+}$) are CORRECT?
optionsEn: Their coordination numbers in aqueous solution and solid complexes are commonly $8$ or $9$ rather than $6$
$\text{Gd}^{3+}$ ($4f^7$) has zero orbital angular momentum ($L = 0$) in its ground state
Both $\text{La}^{3+}$ ($4f^0$) and $\text{Lu}^{3+}$ ($4f^{14}$) are colorless and diamagnetic
Crystal field stabilization energy (CFSE) is the dominant factor determining the geometries of lanthanide complexes
questions.explanationEn: (A) True: large ionic radii and predominantly ionic bonding favor high coordination numbers ($8, 9,$ up to $12$). (B) True: half-filled $4f^7$ has $m_l$ summing to $0$, giving ground state $^8S_{7/2}$ ($L = 0$). (C) True: closed-shell $4f^0$ and $4f^{14}$ have no unpaired electrons and no $f\text{--}f$ transitions. (D) False: $4f$ crystal field splitting is tiny ($\sim 100\text{ cm}^{-1}$), so geometries are governed by steric factors rather than CFSE. Hence (A), (B), and (C) are correct.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Coordination Chemistry & f-Block Elements (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: For the tetrahedral complex $[\text{CoCl}_4]^{2-}$, the crystal field stabilization energy is $-x\Delta_t$. The value of $x$ (rounded off to one decimal place) is _______.
questions.explanationEn: In tetrahedral $[\text{CoCl}_4]^{2-}$, $\text{Co}^{2+}$ has a $3d^7$ configuration. All tetrahedral complexes are high-spin, giving $e^4 t_2^3$. Each $e$ electron contributes $-0.6\Delta_t$ and each $t_2$ electron contributes $+0.4\Delta_t$: $\text{CFSE} = 4(-0.6) + 3(+0.4) = -2.4 + 1.2 = -1.2\Delta_t$. Thus, $x = 1.2$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Coordination Chemistry & f-Block Elements (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: The Racah parameter $B$ for the free $\text{Cr}^{3+}$ ion is $918\text{ cm}^{-1}$, and for $[\text{Cr}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{3+}$ it is $720\text{ cm}^{-1}$. The nephelauxetic ratio $\beta$ (rounded off to two decimal places) is _______.
questions.explanationEn: The nephelauxetic ratio is defined as $\beta = \frac{B_{\text{complex}}}{B_{\text{free ion}}}$. Substituting $B_{\text{complex}} = 720\text{ cm}^{-1}$ and $B_{\text{free ion}} = 918\text{ cm}^{-1}$ gives $\beta = \frac{720}{918} = 0.7843 \approx 0.78$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Coordination Chemistry & f-Block Elements (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: The number of unpaired $5f$ electrons in the $\text{U}^{4+}$ ion (atomic number of $\text{U} = 92$) is _______ (in integer).
questions.explanationEn: Neutral uranium ($Z = 92$) has the ground-state configuration $[\text{Rn}]5f^3 6d^1 7s^2$. Removing four electrons ($7s^2$, $6d^1$, and one $5f$ electron) gives $\text{U}^{4+}$ with $[\text{Rn}]5f^2$, which has $2$ unpaired $5f$ electrons.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Coordination Chemistry & f-Block Elements (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: When an octahedral $[\text{Cu}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{2+}$ complex undergoes tetragonal elongation ($z$-out, $O_h \to D_{4h}$), the correct energy ordering of the $3d$ orbitals from lowest to highest is
questions.explanationEn: In a tetragonal elongation ($z$-out), the two axial ligands move away along $\pm z$ while the four equatorial ligands move closer in the $xy$-plane. Consequently, all orbitals with a $z$-component ($d_{z^2}, d_{xz}, d_{yz}$) are stabilized relative to their in-plane counterparts ($d_{x^2-y^2}, d_{xy}$). Thus, $t_{2g}$ splits into $e_g (d_{xz}, d_{yz}) < b_{2g} (d_{xy})$ and $e_g$ splits into $a_{1g} (d_{z^2}) < b_{1g} (d_{x^2-y^2})$, giving $d_{xz} = d_{yz} < d_{xy} < d_{z^2} < d_{x^2-y^2}$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Coordination Chemistry & f-Block Elements (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: The intense orange-red color ($\lambda_{\max} \approx 452\text{ nm}$, $\varepsilon \approx 14600\text{ M}^{-1}\text{cm}^{-1}$) of $[\text{Ru}(\text{bpy})_3]^{2+}$ ($\text{bpy} = 2,2'$-bipyridine) is attributed to
optionsEn: ligand-to-metal charge transfer (LMCT) from filled $\text{bpy}(\pi)$ orbitals to empty $\text{Ru}(e_g^*)$ orbitals
metal-to-ligand charge transfer (MLCT) from filled $\text{Ru}(t_{2g})$ orbitals to empty $\text{bpy}(\pi^*)$ orbitals
questions.explanationEn: $[\text{Ru}(\text{bpy})_3]^{2+}$ combines an electron-rich, low-valent $4d^6$ $\text{Ru(II)}$ center (filled $t_{2g}^6$ orbitals) with conjugated $\pi$-acceptor bipyridine ligands possessing low-lying empty $\pi^*$ orbitals. Excitation promotes a metal $t_{2g}$ electron into a ligand $\pi^*$ orbital, producing an intense, spin- and Laporte-allowed MLCT band at $452\text{ nm}$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Coordination Chemistry & f-Block Elements (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Substitution of $\text{Cl}^-$ by a nucleophile $\text{Y}$ in a square planar $\text{Pt(II)}$ complex $[\text{PtL}_3\text{Cl}]$ in solvent $\text{S}$ obeys the two-term rate law $\text{Rate} = (k_1 + k_2[\text{Y}])[\text{PtL}_3\text{Cl}]$. The $k_1$ term corresponds to
optionsEn: rate-determining associative attack by solvent $\text{S}$ to form $[\text{PtL}_3\text{S}]$, followed by fast replacement of $\text{S}$ by $\text{Y}$
purely dissociative loss of $\text{Cl}^-$ to form a 3-coordinate $[\text{PtL}_3]^+$ intermediate
direct associative attack of $\text{Y}$ without solvent involvement
questions.explanationEn: In square planar $\text{Pt(II)}$ substitution, both pathways are associative ($I_a$). The $k_2[\text{Y}]$ path represents direct associative attack of $\text{Y}$ on $[\text{PtL}_3\text{Cl}]$, while the $[\text{Y}]$-independent $k_1$ path represents rate-determining associative displacement of $\text{Cl}^-$ by the excess solvent $\text{S}$ (pseudo-first-order) to give $[\text{PtL}_3\text{S}]$, followed by rapid substitution of $\text{S}$ by $\text{Y}$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Coordination Chemistry & f-Block Elements (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Intramolecular racemization of an optically active octahedral tris-chelate complex $[\text{M}(\text{AA})_3]$ without metal-ligand bond cleavage can occur via the Bailar twist or the Ray-Dutt twist. The transition-state geometries of the Bailar twist and the Ray-Dutt twist are, respectively,
questions.explanationEn: In the Bailar twist, one triangular face of the octahedron rotates by $60^\circ$ relative to the opposite face about the $C_3$ axis, passing through a trigonal prismatic ($D_{3h}$) transition state. In the Ray-Dutt (rhombic) twist, one chelate ring remains fixed while the other two twist in opposite directions about a pseudo-$C_3$ axis, passing through a lower-symmetry rhombic ($C_{2v}$) prismatic transition state.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Coordination Chemistry & f-Block Elements (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Although $\text{Ce}^{4+}$ has a $4f^0$ electronic configuration, aqueous solutions of ceric ammonium nitrate, $(\text{NH}_4)_2[\text{Ce}(\text{NO}_3)_6]$, are intensely orange-red. This intense color is caused by
optionsEn: ligand-to-metal charge transfer (LMCT) from oxygen orbitals of $\text{NO}_3^-$/$\text{H}_2\text{O}$ into the empty $4f$ orbitals of $\text{Ce}^{4+}$
questions.explanationEn: Because $\text{Ce}^{4+}$ is $4f^0$, neither $f\text{--}f$ nor MLCT transitions are possible. However, its high $+4$ oxidation state makes $\text{Ce}^{4+}$ a strong oxidant with low-lying empty $4f$ orbitals, enabling an intense, Laporte-allowed ligand-to-metal charge transfer (LMCT) from filled $\text{O}(2p)$ orbitals of the coordinated nitrate/aqua ligands to $\text{Ce}^{4+}$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Coordination Chemistry & f-Block Elements (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statements about Orgel and Tanabe-Sugano (T-S) diagrams are CORRECT?
optionsEn: Orgel diagrams apply only to high-spin (weak-field) complexes, whereas Tanabe-Sugano diagrams cover both weak-field and strong-field regimes including spin-forbidden states

In a Tanabe-Sugano diagram, the horizontal axis is $\Delta_o / B$ and the vertical axis is $E / B$ measured relative to the lowest-energy ground state (which always coincides with the horizontal axis)
Two states of the same symmetry and spin multiplicity (such as $^3T_{1g}(F)$ and $^3T_{1g}(P)$ in octahedral $d^8$) curve away from each other due to the non-crossing rule (configuration interaction)
For octahedral $d^5$, the Tanabe-Sugano diagram has NO discontinuity because high-spin and low-spin states have the same spin multiplicity
questions.explanationEn: (A) True: Orgel diagrams only plot spin-allowed terms of high-spin $D$ and $F$ ions, while T-S diagrams plot all terms across weak and strong fields. (B) True: T-S diagrams plot $E/B$ vs $\Delta_o/B$ with the ground state fixed at $E/B = 0$. (C) True: configuration interaction causes states of identical symmetry and multiplicity to repel and never cross. (D) False: $d^5$ DOES have a discontinuity at $\Delta_o/B \approx 28$ where the ground state switches from $^6A_{1g}$ (HS) to $^2T_{2g}$ (LS). Hence (A), (B), and (C) are correct.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Coordination Chemistry & f-Block Elements (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: In the inner-sphere reduction of $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_5\text{L}]^{n+}$ by $[\text{Cr}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{2+}$, which of the following statements are CORRECT?
optionsEn: For halide bridges, the rate increases in the order $\text{F}^- < \text{Cl}^- < \text{Br}^- < \text{I}^-$ when electron transfer through the bridge is rate-determining, owing to greater polarizability and orbital overlap of softer halides

With $\text{L} = \text{N}_3^-$ (azide), electron transfer is much faster than with $\text{L} = \text{NCS}^-$ or $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ because $\text{N}_3^-$ provides a conjugated $\pi$-pathway between $\text{Cr}$ and $\text{Co}$

With $\text{L} = \text{CN}^-$ (N-bound to Cr in the bridge, $\text{Co}-\text{CN}-\text{Cr}$), linkage isomerization initially produces the metastable N-bonded $[\text{Cr}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_5(\text{NC})]^{2+}$ before rearranging to the C-bonded isomer
Replacing $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_5\text{Cl}]^{2+}$ with $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_6]^{3+}$ accelerates the inner-sphere pathway
questions.explanationEn: (A) True: soft, polarizable halides ($\text{I}^- > \text{Br}^- > \text{Cl}^- > \text{F}^-$) mediate electron transfer more efficiently with the soft-ish $\text{Cr}^{2+}/\text{Co}^{3+}$ pair. (B) True: symmetric conjugated $\text{N}_3^-$ forms a linear bridge with excellent $\pi$-conjugation ($k \approx 3 \times 10^5\text{ M}^{-1}\text{s}^{-1}$). (C) True: attack of $\text{Cr}^{2+}$ at the exposed N end of $\text{Co}-\text{CN}$ yields the kinetic product $[\text{Cr}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_5(\text{NC})]^{2+}$ first. (D) False: $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_6]^{3+}$ has no bridging lone pair and cannot react via an inner-sphere mechanism. Hence (A), (B), and (C) are correct.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Coordination Chemistry & f-Block Elements (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Compute the free-ion ground-state magnetic moment $\mu = g_J\sqrt{J(J+1)}$ (in Bohr magnetons, to two decimal places) expected for dysprosium(III) chloride hexahydrate, $\text{DyCl}_3 \cdot 6\text{H}_2\text{O}$ ($Z_{\text{Dy}} = 66$): _______.
questions.explanationEn: $\text{Dy}^{3+}$ has configuration $[\text{Xe}]4f^9$ (more than half-filled, $5$ unpaired electrons). Thus $S = \frac{5}{2}$, $L = 5$ ($H$), and $J = L + S = \frac{15}{2}$ ($^6H_{15/2}$). The Landé factor is $g_J = 1 + \frac{\frac{15}{2}(\frac{17}{2}) + \frac{5}{2}(\frac{7}{2}) - 5(6)}{2(\frac{15}{2})(\frac{17}{2})} = 1 + \frac{63.75 + 8.75 - 30}{127.5} = 1 + \frac{42.5}{127.5} = \frac{4}{3}$. Therefore, $\mu = \frac{4}{3}\sqrt{63.75} = 10.6458 \approx 10.65\text{ BM}$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Coordination Chemistry & f-Block Elements (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: For the tetrahedral complex $[\text{CoI}_4]^{2-}$ ($^4A_2$ ground state), $\Delta_t = 2700\text{ cm}^{-1}$ and the spin-orbit coupling constant is $\lambda = -178\text{ cm}^{-1}$. Using $\mu_{\text{eff}} = \mu_{\text{so}}\left(1 - \frac{4\lambda}{\Delta_t}\right)$, the calculated effective magnetic moment (in $\text{BM}$, rounded off to two decimal places) is _______.
questions.explanationEn: $\text{Co}^{2+}$ ($d^7$) in tetrahedral $[\text{CoI}_4]^{2-}$ ($e^4 t_2^3$) has $n = 3$ unpaired electrons, giving $\mu_{\text{so}} = \sqrt{3(3+2)} = \sqrt{15} = 3.8730\text{ BM}$. Applying the second-order spin-orbit formula with $\lambda = -178\text{ cm}^{-1}$ and $\Delta_t = 2700\text{ cm}^{-1}$: $\mu_{\text{eff}} = 3.8730\left(1 - \frac{4(-178)}{2700}\right) = 3.8730(1 + 0.26370) = 4.8943 \approx 4.89\text{ BM}$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Coordination Chemistry & f-Block Elements (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: The total number of microstates possible for the $4f^2$ electronic configuration of $\text{Pr}^{3+}$ is _______ (in integer).
questions.explanationEn: The $4f$ subshell has $7$ orbitals and can accommodate at most $N = 2(2l + 1) = 14$ electrons. For $r = 2$ electrons, the total number of microstates is given by the binomial coefficient $\binom{14}{2} = \frac{14!}{2!\,12!} = \frac{14 \times 13}{2} = 91$.
